items.evidence: "Andrei presented the new UniMile rooms"; "The university allocated contiguous rooms on UniMile's sixth floor"; "The plan includes one-, two-, and three-person rooms." Matches Andre's opening and layout description.

The lounge question is reflected ("A reading or lounge room would reduce space available for assigned desks", "Using a two-person room for it would leave 16 positions for 15 people"), but Martin's question on whether the number of people per room is strict, Andre's answer about furniture making three desks in a two-person room doubtful, and the later exchange about squeezing four places into a 3P room are not in the notes.

Furniture and equipment constraints are stated ("Furniture includes a desk, chair, filing cabinet, and possible hanging shelves"; "The group also needs space for a photocopier, fax machine, and printer"). Susan's question about what happens if they do not get the space, and the answers (the rooms are promised; the risk is more people being put in the space) are missing.
The sections "Privacy, working patterns, and room sharing" and "Project grouping and the lounge's purpose" cover the discussion of how to arrange people in the space.

Professors with students ("Confidential discussions can make sharing between professors and their students difficult"), project grouping, phone calls (Susan and Martin), splitting rooms, meeting rooms for projects ("Martin suggested using meeting rooms for project collaboration instead"), visitors, smoking rule, Gisella's placement and admin space are all present. Only the detail of where people can go to smoke (balcony/terrace) is left out.
Nothing in the notes about David's cafeteria question, the reading room not being a cafeteria, or the coffee/vending machines on the first and third floors and the cafeteria closing at five.
"Find out whether the rooms can be separated, including the required authorization (owner: Andrei) [15:30]".
The notes never mention the idea of putting Gisella with the other admin of the school, nor Andre saying "I'll try to find out" / "we'll try" about it (24:34, 25:06).

"Martin said participants should give their own preferences rather than decide for absent colleagues"; "Andrei asked participants to gather preferences and bring a sketch or coherent proposal"; summary says participants will "bring individual preferences".

"Andrei asked participants to gather preferences" loosely covers it, but the notes never state that members should poll the people around them (assistants, colleagues) as Andre asked at 30:12 and 30:41; it is not in the action items.
"Andrei asked participants to ... bring a sketch or coherent proposal"; "planned to bring individual preferences and a draft proposal to a follow-up".

"Another group is developing a separate allocation proposal for later comparison" names the other group, but the notes do not say this group's proposal will be merged with the other one (Andre: "we'll merge it with the other one when the other one is available").
"Ask Maggie and Pierrette about their office preferences (owner: Susan) [30:55]".

"The group discussed meeting the following Tuesday afternoon, around 2 p.m." The transcript shows it was agreed ("about two o'clock? ... Perfect", "Yep. Okay."), but the notes hedge it as "discussed" and leave it out of the action items.

"The group leaned away from project-based seating" and "Project-based seating may not hold up as projects and assignments change." The transcript shows a clear no from Martin and Susan when Andre asked whether anyone was attached to grouping by projects (20:39-20:56), so the notes state it only vaguely.

The notes state "A two-person room was another option, but its second position would need a purpose" and call Gisella's placement unresolved. The transcript supports the notes more than the key: Andre floated a two-person room with the second place for a visitor, Martin objected that a senior visitor could not sit with the secretary, and they settled only on an exchange student or intern as possible, with Andre saying "this sets a bit the stage for Gisella then. We'll try to find out." The notes omit the visitor/intern idea for the second spot.
The notes do not mention the cafeteria question or Martin's answer "We don't have cafeteria" / no money for coffee machines.

Martin's question whether the people-per-room numbers are strict (02:52), Andre's doubt about three desks in a two-person office, and the question of four places in a 3P room (20:14) are not in the notes.

"They did not decide the layout; preferences and constraints still need to be gathered"; "Martin said participants should give their own preferences rather than decide for absent colleagues"; "Susan said professors' preferences should be checked before assigning shared offices."

Both options appear: "Confidential discussions can make sharing between professors and their students difficult" and "Project-based seating may not hold up as projects and assignments change" with "Some staff work across several projects."

"Susan proposed asking whether a two-person room could be split for more privacy" and the action item cover walls; Martin's cubicle suggestion (and Susan rejecting it, wanting four walls) is not mentioned.

The notes discuss the lounge's role ("The lounge could serve as a reading room, meeting space, or overflow workspace"; "Martin said the room's purpose remained an open discussion") and its cost in positions, but never state Susan's question "Do we really need that?" or Andre's answer that many people expressed the need.
"Only one position may remain free for a visitor or intern"; "Susan wanted it to accommodate visitors who need a place to work"; "The group hoped to preserve room for temporary project visitors."
"Gisela's administrative phone work makes room placement a specific constraint. [23:43]"
"A single-person room could accommodate the administrative work"; "A two-person room was another option, but its second position would need a purpose."
No mention of whether there will be a cafeteria.
No mention of the coffee machines on the first and third floors or the cafeteria downstairs closing at five.
